title: Boss: review the launch capacity sheet
summary: A product team sends its capacity sheet for launch. Rebuild its numbers in code, then write the reviewer that flags what a senior would flag.

steps.title: The sheet on your desk
body: The team behind **Snapshare** (short photo captions, example.com) wants sign-off for launch. This is their sheet:
Feed reads per user per day        30
Copies of the data                 1        <- "backups are enough"
Rebuild each number in code, then write the reviewer. Every step is checked by tests.

steps.title: Peak reads and writes
prompt: Write `double PeakReads(long dau, double readsPerUser, double peakFactor)` and
`double PeakWrites(long dau, double writesPerUser, double peakFactor)`: per second at peak,
`dau x perUser / 86,400 x peakFactor`.
With the sheet's own numbers (`8,000,000`, `30` reads, `1` post, peak `1.5`): 4,166.7 reads/s and 138.9 writes/s.
With a realistic peak factor of 3: 8,333.3 and 277.8.
starter: double PeakReads(long dau, double readsPerUser, double peakFactor)
double PeakWrites(long dau, double writesPerUser, double peakFactor)
solution: double PerSecond(long dau, double perUser) => dau * perUser / 86_400;
double PeakReads(long dau, double readsPerUser, double peakFactor) => PerSecond(dau, readsPerUser) * peakFactor;
double PeakWrites(long dau, double writesPerUser, double peakFactor) => PerSecond(dau, writesPerUser) * peakFactor;

steps.title: Storage with growth
prompt: Posts grow every year, so storage is not `rate x years`. Write
`double StorageTbWithGrowth(double writesPerSecYear1, double bytesPerWrite, int years, double yearlyGrowth, int copies)`:
- year 1 writes at `writesPerSecYear1` on average for 365 days;
- each later year writes `(1 + yearlyGrowth)` times the year before (`yearlyGrowth = 1.0` means doubling);
- add up all `years`, multiply by `copies`, and return TB (10^12 bytes).
`StorageTbWithGrowth(100, 1000, 3, 1.0, 3)` is about `66.23`: 3.1536 TB in year 1, then 6.31 and 12.61, times 3 copies.
starter: double StorageTbWithGrowth(double writesPerSecYear1, double bytesPerWrite, int years, double yearlyGrowth, int copies)
solution: double StorageTbWithGrowth(double writesPerSecYear1, double bytesPerWrite, int years, double yearlyGrowth, int copies)
template: Dojo.Eq("no growth is rate x years", 6.31, Math.Round(StorageTbWithGrowth(100, 1000, 2, 0, 1), 2));

steps.title: How many servers?
prompt: Write `int Servers(double peakQps, double cpuMsPerRequest, int coresPerServer, double targetUtil, int spareServers)`:
the servers needed so the busy cores (`peakQps x cpuMs / 1,000`) run at `targetUtil`, **rounded up** to whole
servers, plus `spareServers` (for a lost server or a deploy).
`Servers(10000, 12, 8, 0.5, 1)` is `31`: 120 busy cores, 240 at 50%, 30 servers of 8 cores, plus 1 spare.
starter: int Servers(double peakQps, double cpuMsPerRequest, int coresPerServer, double targetUtil, int spareServers)
solution: int Servers(double peakQps, double cpuMsPerRequest, int coresPerServer, double targetUtil, int spareServers)
template: Dojo.Eq("10k QPS, 12 ms, 8 cores, 50%, 1 spare", 31, Servers(10_000, 12, 8, 0.5, 1));
Dojo.Eq("5k QPS, 9 ms, 16 cores, 75%, 1 spare", 5, Servers(5_000, 9, 16, 0.75, 1));
Dojo.Eq("tiny load still needs one server", 3, Servers(1, 1, 8, 0.5, 2));

steps.title: The reviewer
prompt: Write `List<string> Review(Sheet s)` that returns the problems a senior would flag, **in this order**, using
exactly these messages (an empty list when nothing is wrong):
1. `PeakFactor < 2` -> `"peak factor below 2x"`
2. `TargetUtil > 0.75` -> `"target utilisation above 75%"`
3. `SpareServers < 1` -> `"no spare server for a failure or a deploy"`
4. `Copies < 2` -> `"a single copy of the data"`
5. `SloPercent >= 99.99` -> `"99.99% needs automated failover across zones: justify it"`
The record is declared by the tests:
```csharp
record Sheet(double PeakFactor, double TargetUtil, int SpareServers, int Copies, double SloPercent);
Snapshare's sheet (1.5, 0.9, 0, 1, 99.99) fails all five.
solution: if (s.SpareServers < 1) problems.Add("no spare server for a failure or a deploy");
if (s.Copies < 2) problems.Add("a single copy of the data");
if (s.SloPercent >= 99.99) problems.Add("99.99% needs automated failover across zones: justify it");
template: Dojo.Eq("Snapshare v3 fails everything", new List<string> { "peak factor below 2x", "target utilisation above 75%", "no spare server for a failure or a deploy", "a single copy of the data", "99.99% needs automated failover across zones: justify it" }, Review(new Sheet(1.5, 0.9, 0, 1, 99.99)));
Dojo.Eq("a sound sheet passes", new List<string>(), Review(new Sheet(3, 0.6, 2, 3, 99.9)));
Dojo.Eq("boundaries are fine", new List<string>(), Review(new Sheet(2, 0.75, 1, 2, 99.95)));
Dojo.Eq("only the copies", new List<string> { "a single copy of the data" }, Review(new Sheet(2.5, 0.7, 1, 1, 99.9)));
Dojo.Eq("utilisation and spares", new List<string> { "target utilisation above 75%", "no spare server for a failure or a deploy" }, Review(new Sheet(3, 0.8, 0, 3, 99.5)));
record Sheet(double PeakFactor, double TargetUtil, int SpareServers, int Copies, double SloPercent);
